doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

title: Brother Norman's 78 records and early listening
summary: His brother Norman had 78s he called killers, including Billy Taylor, Lester Young and Charlie Parker, and a friend Nicky Hill who scatted well.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Was there moments of, “All right, Roscoe, come and listen to this.” Did he have people that he chose for you to hear back then?

Well I mean yeah, he had his list, but more on that side was my brother Norman. Norman, he had all these 78 records, and he called them “killers.” He’d say, “Come on over here bruh” and listen to this and listen to that and so on. And that kind of thing. I don’t know if you’re familiar with the saxophonist Nicky Hill? He was a prominent saxophonist in Chicago you know, and he was friends with Nicky Hill. And he was a very good scatter, you know, a very good scatter. So I would listen to him do that. But he had all these 78 records you know, and then so he would sit me down and have me listen, I remember some things from Billy Taylor, you know, Lester Young, and on and on. Charlie Parker of course. And so that’s what got me into paying more attention to the music you know.
